note.text: A lit triple whose complement is dark holds both nexioms. If any single in it lights, needs=one: that object is a nexiom; find the other by pairing it with each remaining object in the triple. If no single lights, needs=two. Then test pairs inside the lit triple: the unique lighting pair is the answer. You need not test the last pair—if the other two pairs are dark, it is the answer. A dark triple never holds both. If both triples are dark, needs=two and the nexioms are split one per triple; test cross-pairs, swapping one side when dark. Singles never light when needs=two.
